findings.title: README and the commands page still say an AI-initiated apply or archive always asks first
findings.recommendation: Give both sentences the clause task 5.1 gave docs/customization.md, docs/workflow-engine.md, docs/getting-started.md and docs/concepts.md: docs/commands.md:8-9 becomes "When the AI arrives at `apply`, `archive` or `bulk-archive` by any route other than your typing it or your `chain` setting granting it, it asks before writing anything; `bulk-archive` is never granted.", and README.md:52-54's last clause becomes "an AI-initiated apply or archive your `chain` setting does not grant asks first". Then grep README.md and docs/ once more for "asks first" and "asks before".
findings.reproduction: With chain: {apply: true} in orbit/config.yaml, a walk whose next command is `/orbit:apply <change> — user-invoked` chains into apply, and apply's Step 0 granted bullet records consent "setting" and fires no consent prompt (src/core/templates/workflows/apply-change.ts, Step 0). docs/commands.md:8-9 tells the reader that apply reached 'by any route other than your typing it' asks before writing anything, and README.md:52-54 that 'an AI-initiated apply or archive asks first'; both are now false for a granted arrival. The change corrected the same claim in docs/concepts.md:260-261 and docs/customization.md:258 but not these two.

findings.title: A granted archive meets a HEAD-vs-attachment mismatch as one printed line, with nobody asked
findings.recommendation: Decide how a granted archive meets Step 0.7's mismatch. Today the mismatch rides in the consent preview on a prompted arrival (where Abort is one click away) and is one line before Step 1 otherwise; a granted arrival therefore syncs, moves and emits on the wrong branch, and the tail then skips with its recovery note, leaving the archive's writes uncommitted on a branch that may be the default one. The behaviour equals a typed archive's, which the engine-gates row promises, but a typed archive has the user at the keyboard and a granted one may not.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: On a granted arrival, make a Step 0.7 mismatch a decision prompt (switch first, or proceed, or abort): add its row to orbit-conventions' `A chain treats each prompt by its kind` and tag the site `(chain: decision)`, so the chain stops before any archive write.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Keep it, and name it as a limit in orbit-archive-modifications' `Consent prompt on AI-mediated archive entry`: a granted archive with HEAD off the attachment's branch writes locally and its tail skips, recoverable by the tail's note.

findings.title: The chain row's key list keeps an "and" from its three-key form
findings.recommendation: Read the list as five items: "`review` (...), `review-external` (...), `address-reviews` (the walk), `apply` (...) and `archive` (...)" — drop the "and" before `address-reviews` and put a comma there.

commentary: The engine half is small and exact: two rows in CHAIN_KEY_TABLE, chainKeyFor collapsed onto chainTargetFor, and validateConsent placed beside validatePayload, reading the same resolveChainSetting the chain object reads, so the entry and the gate share one definition of granted. I checked the next_command producer in instruction-loader.ts: mid-apply the engine names `/orbit:apply <change> — user-invoked` again, so with chain.apply a chunked apply chains chunk to chunk as fresh granted invocations, each bounded by the no-progress row because every chunk writes an emit; that reads as intended. Both Step 0s classify a granted arrival from the engine's object and never from the route, the archive body states the tag rules itself without a parenthesised tag the scanner would read, and the prompt inventory in chain-prompt-tags.test.ts matches the table row for row. The unplanned src/core/pr/tail.ts change (observations.carried_untracked) implements a baseline scenario that was never true; I read its pre-move tracked set (HEAD tree plus index) against the tests for a staged and an unstaged move, and it holds, with the archive emit correctly excluded. One reading came from the live checkout, which equals HEAD here: the build, the full suite (187 files, 3992 tests, no FAIL), validate --strict, validate --sources and the scenario map (109 delta scenarios, 0 uncovered). The residue the change left is in prose, not code: two user-facing docs still promise a prompt the grant now removes.

direction.reasoning: The grant does what the specs say, and the write gate holds the one value it can check. What remains is prose: two docs sentences that a reader setting chain.apply would find false, which a walk fixes in two edits. The HEAD-mismatch question is a design choice the user may settle either way, and it does not need to hold up the archive.
